title: West Flanders Squares — Bruges, Damme and Veurne

bestPeriod.note: Start on a Saturday so the Wednesday market at Veurne and the Saturday market at 't Zand both land inside the week.

summary: Four nights in Bruges and three in Veurne, moving by train and towpath, built around lace workshops and two of Flanders' best market squares.
hook: Bruges is not ruined by its visitors; it is simply borrowed by them between 10:00 and 18:00. Stay four nights, learn the timings, and the city hands itself back twice a day. Then move an hour west to Veurne, where the Grote Markt is one of the most complete squares in Flanders and nobody is queuing for anything.

snapshot.Total Distance / Terrain: One 60 km rail relocation; 30–40 km walked, plus an optional 14 km canal bike ride. Entirely flat
snapshot.Getting There: Brussels Airport to Bruges by train, approx. 1h30 with one change; Bruges to Veurne via Lichtervelde, approx. 1h
snapshot.Who It Suits: Museum-goers, lace and craft people, beer drinkers, anyone who wants a walkable week without a car

itinerary.title: Arrival, and the two squares that matter
itinerary.morning: Train from Brussels Airport to Bruges. If you land early enough to be in town before 14:00 on a Saturday, walk straight to 't Zand, where the city's largest weekly market runs roughly 07:00–14:00 across the whole plein — flowers, cheese, fish, and the rotisserie vans.
itinerary.afternoon: Learn the geography with your feet. The Markt is the big one, hemmed by the Belfort and the neo-Gothic Provinciaal Hof. Step through to the Burg next door, which is smaller, older and better: the Stadhuis of 1376 with its gilded façade, and the Heilig-Bloedbasiliek stacked in two chapels, Romanesque below and Gothic above.
itinerary.evening: Walk east to Jan van Eyckplein and the old Hanseatic quarter, then south along the Groenerei. Dinner in the Sint-Anna district, five minutes and a world away from the Markt.
itinerary.dayStats: Towns visited: 1. Walking: 6 km. Transfer time: approx. 1h30 from Brussels.

itinerary.title: The poplar road to Damme
itinerary.morning: Nothing before 10:00. Then rent bikes — Fietsen Popelier on Mariastraat is the long-standing option — and ride the Damse Vaart, the dead-straight Napoleonic canal lined with poplars, 7 km northeast to Damme. In season the *Lamme Goedzak* paddle boat does the same trip from Noorweegse Kaai if you prefer to sit.
itinerary.afternoon: Damme is a medieval port that lost its sea. The Marktplein holds the 1464 Stadhuis and the statue of Jacob van Maerlant, and the village is officially a *boekendorp* — a book village. On the second Sunday of the month, March to October, secondhand booksellers set up on the square from about 10:00 to 18:00.
itinerary.evening: Eel in green sauce — *paling in 't groen* — is the local dish, and Siphon on the Damse Vaart-Oost has been serving it for generations. Book. Ride back into a Flanders sunset on a flat towpath.
itinerary.dayStats: Towns visited: 2. Walking: 3 km. Cycling: 14 km. Transfer time: 30 min each way by bike.

itinerary.title: Lace, brick and beer
itinerary.morning: Take the local train seven minutes north to Lissewege, a whitewashed village under an unfinished brick tower. Walk 1.5 km out to the Ter Doest tithe barn, a 13th-century Cistercian brick hall the size of a church, and one of the great pieces of Flemish agricultural building.
itinerary.afternoon: Back in Bruges, go to the Kantcentrum on Balstraat, where lacemakers demonstrate bobbin work Monday to Saturday afternoons, roughly 14:00–17:00. Bruges lace means *bloemwerk* — flower work — and Duchesse; watch the pins go in and you will stop asking why a collar costs €400. 't Apostelientje across the street sells the real thing beside the machine-made imports so you can learn the difference by eye.
itinerary.evening: Brouwerij De Halve Maan on Walplein, brewing Brugse Zot in the centre since 1856, pipes its beer to the bottling plant through a 3.2 km underground pipeline. Tour, then drink somewhere better lit: 't Brugs Beertje on Kemelstraat keeps a serious list.
itinerary.dayStats: Towns visited: 2. Walking: 8 km. Transfer time: 15 min return by rail.

itinerary.title: Memling morning, canal afternoon
itinerary.morning: Another late start; nothing before 10:00. The Vismarkt colonnade holds a small fish market Tuesday to Saturday, roughly 08:00–13:00, and it is a two-minute detour on the way to the Sint-Janshospitaal, where six Memling panels including the Ursula shrine sit in the hospital they were painted for.
itinerary.afternoon: The Groeningemuseum, ten minutes away, holds Van Eyck's *Madonna with Canon van der Paele* and Bosch's *Last Judgement*. Both museums close on Mondays, which is why they sit here.
itinerary.evening: Walk the Begijnhof and Minnewater at dusk, then climb the Kruisvest embankment to the Sint-Janshuismolen, a working windmill on the old ramparts. The Markt is bearable again after 18:00.
itinerary.dayStats: Towns visited: 1. Walking: 7 km. Transfer time: none.

itinerary.title: Market day in Veurne
itinerary.morning: This is the one early start of the week and it earns it. Take the 08:00-ish train from Bruges via Lichtervelde and you are in Veurne inside an hour, with the Wednesday market still running on the Grote Markt until about 13:00. Buy lunch there.
itinerary.afternoon: The Grote Markt is an almost intact 16th–17th-century ensemble: the Stadhuis with its loggia, the Landhuis with the belfry behind, the Spaans Paviljoen, and the Vleeshuis. Sint-Walburgakerk sits in a walled close just off it. This is the square Bruges' visitors never reach.
itinerary.evening: Veurne after dark is very quiet. Eat on the square, then look for the plaques marking the route of the Boeteprocessie, the barefoot penitents' procession held on the last Sunday of July since the 17th century.
itinerary.dayStats: Towns visited: 2. Walking: 5 km. Transfer time: approx. 1h by rail.

itinerary.title: Hops and abbey beer
itinerary.morning: Bus or drive 25 km south to Poperinge, the centre of Belgian hop growing. The Hopmuseum on Gasthuisstraat occupies the old municipal hop-drying and weighing hall and explains the whole crop cycle; the Grote Markt outside holds its weekly market on Friday mornings.
itinerary.afternoon: Ten minutes further is Westvleteren, where In de Vrede is the visitor café of the Sint-Sixtus abbey. It is the only place you can reliably sit down with the abbey's Trappist beer without a phone reservation for the collection line. Cheese, pâté and one glass; the beer is 10.2% and you are not driving.
itinerary.evening: Continue to Ieper for the Last Post, sounded under the Menin Gate at 20:00 every single evening since 1928. Then back to Veurne, half an hour north.
itinerary.dayStats: Towns visited: 3. Walking: 5 km. Transfer time: approx. 1h30 total by road.

itinerary.title: Ovens, dunes, departure
itinerary.morning: The Bakkerijmuseum on Albert I-laan in Veurne is a working bakery museum with wood-fired ovens and a genuinely good reason to arrive hungry. Slow morning, no rush.
itinerary.afternoon: Eight minutes by train to De Panne, then the Kusttram — the 67 km coastal tram that runs the entire Belgian shoreline — a few stops north along the Westhoek dunes. Walk the dune paths, eat shrimp croquettes, get sand in your shoes.
itinerary.evening: Train back east for Brussels, roughly 2h15 from Veurne with a change.
itinerary.dayStats: Towns visited: 2. Walking: 6 km. Transfer time: approx. 2h15 to Brussels.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Ter Reien
accommodationStrategy.description: Sits on the Langestraat where two canals meet, in the Sint-Anna quarter — inside the old town, but on the residential side of it, so you walk five minutes to the Burg and sleep somewhere silent. Rooms over the water are the ones worth paying for. Bike storage on site, which matters for the Damme day.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 2–3 months ahead for May, June and September weekends.

accommodationStrategy.name: Guesthouse Nuit Blanche
accommodationStrategy.description: An alternative for a couple who want the smallest possible operation: a handful of rooms in a historic house on the Groeninge canal, a minute from the museum quarter. No lobby, no groups, no lift. Breakfast is brought to you.
accommodationStrategy.booking: 3–4 months ahead; it sells out first.

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel 't Kasteel en 't Koetshuys
accommodationStrategy.description: A small hotel in a nineteenth-century house and its coach house on the edge of Veurne's centre, five minutes' walk from the Grote Markt and the station. Parking on site if you hire a car for the Poperinge day, and a garden that makes the two slow evenings here work.

logistics.emergency: 112 for everything. Belgium also runs 101 for police and 1733 for the out-of-hours doctor service.
logistics.money: Bancontact and cards work nearly everywhere. Market stalls, the abbey café at Westvleteren and small bakeries prefer cash; carry €40–€60.

other.label: Museum closures
other.text: Most Musea Brugge sites, including the Groeningemuseum and Sint-Janshospitaal, close on Mondays. Build your indoor day around Tuesday to Sunday. The Musea Brugge Card covers the group of them for three days and pays back after roughly three visits.

other.label: The Belfort has a capacity limit
other.text: The stair takes a fixed number at a time and tickets are timed; book online the day before, early slot.

other.label: Trains
other.text: SNCB/NMBS runs hourly to Veurne with a tight change at Lichtervelde; the last useful westbound train leaves Bruges before 21:00. Buy in the app.

other.label: Bikes on trains
other.text: Bikes need a supplement and are barred from some peak services; hire in Bruges for the Damme ride. Drone flight over the historic core is prohibited.

other.label: Opening-hour traps
other.text: Flemish kitchens close early — last orders at 21:00 is normal. Many family restaurants shut two weekdays, often Monday and Tuesday, and rarely advertise it; have your hotel phone ahead the same morning.

proTips: The Markt and Burg are effectively empty before 09:00 and after 18:30. Do your photographs and your coffee then, and put museums and lace in the middle of the day when the streets are worst.
Ride the canal to Damme and take the *Lamme Goedzak* back, or the reverse — but check the boat's limited schedule before committing.
At the Kantcentrum, arrive at 14:00 sharp when the lacemakers sit down. By 16:00 the demonstration tables are thinning out.
Ask at In de Vrede whether the abbey shop is selling that day. Availability rotates and is announced locally; the café itself always has the beer on the list.
Veurne's Wednesday market packs up hard at 13:00. Eat there rather than planning lunch afterwards, when the town is quiet.
Buy a De Lijn day pass before boarding the Kusttram; onboard fares cost noticeably more.

packingNotes: A rain shell you would happily wear all day. West Flanders gets drizzle in every month.
Shoes for cobbles that have been polished by six centuries of feet — Bruges is genuinely slippery when wet.
A windproof layer for the Westhoek dunes, always colder than inland.
Cash in small notes for markets and the abbey café.
Something flat and soft to carry lace home in; it must not be creased over a hard edge.
whatCouldGoWrong: **Bruges is unbearably crowded.** The city takes cruise-excursion traffic from Zeebrugge on some days. If the centre is impossible, take the seven-minute train to Lissewege or the towpath to Damme and come back at six.
**Rain all week.** The indoor programme absorbs four days: Groeningemuseum, Sint-Janshospitaal, Kantcentrum, De Halve Maan, the Hopmuseum and the Bakkerijmuseum.
**You miss the Lichtervelde connection.** Trains to Veurne are hourly; the fallback is the coastal tram from Ostend, slower but scenic, or a taxi from Diksmuide.
**Westvleteren has no beer to sell.** It regularly does not. In de Vrede still pours it by the glass, and any decent Bruges beer café will have Trappist alternatives — Rochefort, Westmalle, Orval.
